**Short description**: 2022 NFT plagiarism controversy [![Image 1](https://handwiki.org/wiki/images/thumb/9/9b/15chill.png/330px-15chill.png)](https://handwiki.org/wiki/File:15chill.png) 15 (ponysona pictured) discovered that Voiceverse had used [15.ai](https://handwiki.org/wiki/15.ai "15.ai") to generate voice lines that were used to market Voiceverse's partnership with Troy Baker and subsequently sold as NFTs. In January 2022, 15—the pseudonymous [Massachusetts Institute of Technology](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Organization:Massachusetts_Institute_of_Technology "Organization:Massachusetts Institute of Technology") (MIT) artificial intelligence researcher and creator of the non-commercial [generative artificial intelligence](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence "Generative artificial intelligence") voice synthesis research project [15.ai](https://handwiki.org/wiki/15.ai "15.ai")—discovered that the [blockchain](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Finance:Blockchain "Finance:Blockchain")\-based technology company **Voiceverse** had [plagiarized](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Social:Plagiarism "Social:Plagiarism") from their platform. Voiceverse marketed itself as a service that offered [AI voice cloning technology](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Audio_deepfake "Audio deepfake") that could be purchased and traded as [non-fungible tokens](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Finance:Non-fungible_token "Finance:Non-fungible token") (NFTs). Amid heightened controversy over NFTs in the gaming industry, voice actor Troy Baker (who has been described as one of the most famous voice actors in video games) announced his partnership with Voiceverse on January 14, 2022, triggering immediate backlash over concerns about the [environmental impact of NFTs](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Finance:Non-fungible_token#Environmental_concerns "Finance:Non-fungible token"), [potential for fraud](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Finance:Non-fungible_token#Plagiarism_and_fraud "Finance:Non-fungible token"), [predatory monetization in video games](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Finance:Video_game_monetization#Criticism "Finance:Video game monetization"), and the potential of [AI displacing jobs for human voice actors](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Technological_unemployment "Engineering:Technological unemployment"). Later that same day, 15 revealed through server logs that Voiceverse had generated voice lines using 15's free text-to-speech platform, pitch-shifted the audio to make them unrecognizable, and [falsely marketed](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Finance:False_advertising "Finance:False advertising") the samples as their own technology before selling them as NFTs. Within an hour of being confronted with evidence, Voiceverse confessed and stated that their marketing team had used 15.ai without proper attribution while rushing to create a technology demo to coincide with Baker's partnership announcement, further exacerbating the already negative reception to the original announcement. In response, 15 replied "Go fuck yourself"; the interaction went [viral](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Viral_phenomenon "Viral phenomenon") and garnered a large amount of support for the developer. News publications universally characterized this incident as Voiceverse having "stolen" from 15.ai. The next day, Baker appeared on a [podcast](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Podcast "Podcast") and stated that his motivation had been to help independent creators who were unable to afford professional voice actors. Following continued backlash and the plagiarism revelation, Baker ended his partnership with Voiceverse on January 31, 2022. Subsequently, the incident was documented in multiple AI ethics databases, criticisms of predatory monetization in video games, and retrospectives as an instance of plagiarism and theft stemming from artificial intelligence. Background ---------- ### Troy Baker [![Image 2](https://handwiki.org/wiki/images/thumb/3/3b/Troy_Baker_%2853616263785%29.jpg/250px-Troy_Baker_%2853616263785%29.jpg)](https://handwiki.org/wiki/File:Troy_Baker_/(53616263785/).jpg) Troy Baker in 2024 Troy Baker is a prominent voice actor in the [video game industry](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Video_game_industry "Video game industry") best known for his performances as Joel Miller in [_The Last of Us_ franchise](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Software:The_Last_of_Us_/(franchise/) "Software:The Last of Us (franchise)").[\[1\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-Peters-2022-1) Baker has been described as "ubiquitous" by _Polygon_,[\[2\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-McWhertor-2022-2) "one of the most high-profile and prolific voice actors in video games" by _Eurogamer_,[\[3\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-Phillips-2022-3) and "arguably the most famous voice actor in the gaming industry" by _GameGuru_.[\[4\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-Kuchkanov-2022-4) His other prominent roles include voicing Agent John "Jonesy" Jones in _[Fortnite](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Software:Fortnite "Software:Fortnite")_, Booker DeWitt in _[BioShock Infinite](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Software:BioShock_Infinite "Software:BioShock Infinite")_, and both Batman and Joker in multiple Batman video games.[\[2\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-McWhertor-2022-2)[\[3\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-Phillips-2022-3) As of October 2025, Baker holds the record for the most acting nominations at the BAFTA Games Awards, with five between 2013 and 2021.[\[5\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-5) ### Voiceverse Voiceverse is a [blockchain](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Finance:Blockchain "Finance:Blockchain")\-based startup founded by the Bored Ape Yacht Club[\[6\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-McKean-2022-6) that marketed itself as offering AI voice cloning technology in the form of NFTs.[\[7\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-Makuch-2022-7) Prior to the announcement of their partnership with Baker, Voiceverse had partnered with LOVO, Inc., an AI voice platform that, according to LOVO, could generate human-like voices.[\[2\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-McWhertor-2022-2) Voiceverse stated that any user who purchases a voice NFT would have unlimited and perpetual access to the voice model,[\[2\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-McWhertor-2022-2) which could be used to create content such as [audiobooks](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Audiobook "Engineering:Audiobook"), YouTube videos, [podcasts](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Podcast "Podcast"), e-learning materials, in-game voice chat, and Zoom calls.[\[3\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-Phillips-2022-3)[\[7\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-Makuch-2022-7) Voiceverse promised that buyers would "OWN _\[sic\]_ all of the [IP](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Social:Intellectual_property "Social:Intellectual property")" of content they created using these voices.[\[2\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-McWhertor-2022-2) Voiceverse's roadmap included plans to release 8,888 initial voice NFTs, a feature to add emotions to existing voices, and the ability for users to mint their own voices as NFTs. Prior to Baker's partnership, Voiceverse had also partnered with voice actors Charlet Chung, who voices D.Va in _[Overwatch](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Software:Overwatch "Software:Overwatch")_,[\[2\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-McWhertor-2022-2) and Andy Milonakis of _The Andy Milonakis Show_.[\[2\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-McWhertor-2022-2)[\[7\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-Makuch-2022-7) ### 15.ai [15.ai](https://handwiki.org/wiki/15.ai "15.ai") is a free web application launched in 2020 that uses [artificial intelligence](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence "Artificial intelligence") to generate text-to-speech voices of fictional characters from popular media.[\[8\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-8) Created by a [pseudonymous](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Pseudonym "Pseudonym") artificial intelligence researcher known as 15, who began developing the technology as a [freshman](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Social:Freshman "Social:Freshman") during their undergraduate research at MIT, it was an early example of an application of [generative artificial intelligence](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence "Generative artificial intelligence") during the initial stages of the [AI boom](https://handwiki.org/wiki/AI_boom "AI boom"). The platform showed that deep neural networks could generate emotionally expressive speech with only 15 seconds of speech; the name "15.ai" references the creator's statement that a voice can be convincingly cloned with just 15 seconds of audio, as opposed to the tens of hours of data previously required. 15.ai became an Internet phenomenon in early 2021 when content utilizing it went viral on [social media](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Social:Social_media "Social:Social media") and quickly gained widespread use among various Internet fandoms. 15 has emphasized that it remain free and non-commercial; it only requires users to give proper credit when using the service for content creation.[\[9\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-9) ### NFTs in the video game industry By early 2022, NFTs had become highly controversial within the gaming industry.[\[6\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-McKean-2022-6) Critics raised concerns about their environmental impact due to the significant energy consumption of blockchain technology.[\[6\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-McKean-2022-6) In addition, the prevalence of scams, fraud, and potential [money laundering](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Finance:Money_laundering "Finance:Money laundering") associated with NFT sales, as well as fears that NFTs were a new form of [predatory monetization](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Finance:Video_game_monetization#Criticism "Finance:Video game monetization") following the increasing frequency of loot boxes, caused vocal pushback from the gaming community.[\[6\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-McKean-2022-6) Several major gaming companies had begun exploring NFT integration into their products, though fan backlash had already forced some projects to be cancelled.[\[10\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-Bankhurst-2022-10) On December 16, 2021,[\[11\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-11) the developers of _[Software:S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2: Heart of Chernobyl](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Software:S.T.A.L.K.E.R._2:_Heart_of_Chernobyl "Software:S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2: Heart of Chernobyl")_ announced that they would be including NFTs in the game, but cancelled within an hour of the announcement due to immediate universal backlash.[\[10\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-Bankhurst-2022-10)[\[1\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-Peters-2022-1) Simultaneously, the rise of AI voice technology raised concerns among voice actors about potential job displacement and the devaluation of their work amidst the voice acting industry's ongoing struggles for better compensation and working conditions.[\[6\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-McKean-2022-6)[\[12\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-Brown-2022-12)[\[2\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-McWhertor-2022-2) Partnership announcement and backlash ------------------------------------- >
Troy BakerTwitter
@TroyBakerVA
> > I'm partnering with @VoiceverseNFT to explore ways where together we might bring new tools to new creators to make new things, and allow everyone a chance to own & invest in the IP's they create. We all have a story to tell. You can hate. Or you can create. What'll it be? > > January 14, 2022, 1:02 a.m.[\[12\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-Brown-2022-12) On January 14, 2022, 1:02 a.m. EST, Baker announced on [Twitter](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Company:Twitter "Company:Twitter") that he was partnering with Voiceverse "to explore ways where together we might bring new tools to new creators to make new things, and allow everyone a chance to own & invest in the IP's they create." The announcement concluded with the statement "You can hate. Or you can create."[\[2\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-McWhertor-2022-2)[\[12\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-Brown-2022-12) Baker's specific role with Voiceverse remained unclear at the time of the announcement.[\[2\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-McWhertor-2022-2) [File:Chubbiverse promotional video.webm](https://handwiki.org/wiki/File:Chubbiverse_promotional_video.webm "File:Chubbiverse promotional video.webm") Along with Baker's announcement, Voiceverse promoted their supposed voice AI technology on Twitter by posting animated videos that featured a cat character created by NFT firm **Chubbiverse**.[\[13\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-Phillips-2022-2-13)[\[14\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-Innes-2022-14) The videos concluded with text that read "The Voice Powered By Voiceverse"; Voiceverse stated on Twitter that the voices in the animations had been generated using their own AI voice synthesis technology and presented the videos as a [technology demonstration](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Technology_demonstration "Engineering:Technology demonstration") of their voice NFT the parent company of Voiceverse, alleging that LOVO had illegally copied the voices of voice actors and used them without permission. Court documents cited LOVO/Voiceverse's prior plagiarism of 15.ai as part of the case.[\[49\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-59)[\[33\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-courtcase-36) In April 2021, LOVO wrote that "\[15.ai\] are LOVO's competition because we do all of that as well, but none of us are real threats to each other, yet."[\[50\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-60) Legacy ------ The incident was documented by various organizations indexing [ethics violations in artificial intelligence](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Philosophy:Ethics_of_artificial_intelligence "Philosophy:Ethics of artificial intelligence") and [cryptocurrency](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Finance:Non-fungible_token#Plagiarism_and_fraud "Finance:Non-fungible token"). Both the AI Incident Database (AIID) and the AI, Algorithmic, and Automation Incidents and Controversies (AIAAIC)[\[lower-alpha 8\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-62) classified the incident as theft.[\[31\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-AIAAIC-34)[\[24\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-Sonali-2022-27) Later, the AIAAIC also formally classified the incident as a case of [plagiarism](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Social:Plagiarism "Social:Plagiarism").[\[31\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-AIAAIC-34) The MIT AI Risk Repository catalogued the incident as an example of "economic and cultural devaluation of human effort".[\[24\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-Sonali-2022-27) In a retrospective of the incident in her _Web3 Is Going Just Great_ website, writer and crypto skeptic Molly White wrote that "things were further soured when it was revealed that Voiceverse had stolen work without crediting it from \[...\] 15.ai." White categorized the incident as theft, a "bad idea", and "shady business".[\[52\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-White-2022-63) In an article about [video game monetization](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Finance:Video_game_monetization "Finance:Video game monetization") on the Russian educational platform _Skillbox_, video game journalist Pavel Khibchenko described the plagiarism incident as an example of [fraud in NFTs](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Finance:Non-fungible_token#Plagiarism_and_fraud "Finance:Non-fungible token").[\[53\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-64) In 2023, _/Film_ described the incident as plagiarism and referred to Baker's partnership with Voiceverse as "one of \[his\] less reputable roles", writing that "nobody's perfect."[\[54\]](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Voiceverse_NFT_plagiarism_scandal#cite_note-65) See also -------- * Ponzi scheme * Video game controversies * [Artificial intelligence controversies](https://handwiki.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence_controversies "Artificial intelligence controversies") Notes ----- 1. [![Image 1](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/09/NFT_diagram.svg/500px-NFT_diagram.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:NFT_diagram.svg)

Illustration of a non-fungible token generated by a [smart contract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_contract "Smart contract") (a program designed to automatically execute contract terms)

A **non-fungible token** (**NFT**) is a unique digital identifier that is recorded on a [blockchain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockchain "Blockchain") and is used to certify ownership and authenticity. It cannot be copied, substituted, or subdivided.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-1) The ownership of an NFT is recorded in the blockchain and can be transferred by the owner, allowing NFTs to be sold and traded. Initially pitched in 2017 as a new class of [investment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Investment "Investment") asset, by September 2023 one report claimed that over 95% of NFT collections had zero [monetary value](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monetary_value "Monetary value").[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-Yang2023-2)[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-Vigliarolo2023-3)

NFTs can be created by anybody and require little or no coding skill to create. NFTs typically contain references to [digital files](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_file "Digital file") such as artworks, photos, videos, and audio. Because NFTs are uniquely identifiable, they differ from [cryptocurrencies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptocurrencies "Cryptocurrencies"), which are [fungible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungible "Fungible") (hence the name non-fungible token).

Proponents claim that NFTs provide a public [certificate of authenticity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Certificate_of_authenticity "Certificate of authenticity") or [proof of ownership](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Title_/(property/) "Title (property)"), but the legal rights conveyed by an NFT can be uncertain. The ownership of an NFT as defined by the blockchain has no inherent legal meaning and does not necessarily grant [copyright](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copyright "Copyright"), [intellectual property](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intellectual_property "Intellectual property") rights, or other legal rights over its associated digital file. An NFT does not restrict the sharing or copying of its associated digital file and does not prevent the creation of NFTs that reference identical files.

NFT trading increased from US$82 million in 2020 to US$17 billion in 2021.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-4) NFTs have been used as [speculative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speculation "Speculation") investments and have drawn criticism for the energy cost and [carbon footprint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbon_footprint "Carbon footprint") associated with some types of blockchain, as well as their use in [art scams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confidence_trick "Confidence trick").[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-5) The NFT market has also been compared to an [economic bubble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_bubble "Economic bubble") or a [Ponzi scheme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ponzi_scheme "Ponzi scheme").[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-6) In 2022, the NFT market collapsed; a May 2022 estimate was that the number of sales was down over 90% compared to 2021.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-flatlining-7)

Characteristics
---------------

An NFT is a data file, stored on a type of digital ledger called a blockchain, which can be sold and traded.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-8) The NFT can be associated with a particular asset – digital or physical – such as an image, art, music, or recording of a sports event.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-9) It may confer licensing rights to use the asset for a specified purpose.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-$69_million_for_digital_art?-10) An NFT (and, if applicable, the associated license to use, copy, or display the underlying asset) can be traded and sold on digital markets.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-Kastrenakes-11) However, the extralegal nature of NFT trading usually results in an informal exchange of ownership over the asset that has no legal basis for enforcement,[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-Mendis-2021-12) and so often confers little more than use as a status symbol.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-vice_right-clicker-13)

NFTs function like [cryptographic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptographic "Cryptographic") tokens, but unlike cryptocurrencies, NFTs are not usually mutually interchangeable, so they are not [fungible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungible "Fungible").[\[a\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-15) A non-fungible token contains data links, for example which point to details about where the associated art is stored, that can be affected by [link rot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Link_rot "Link rot").[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-16)

### Copyright

[![Image 2: NFT is ownable, the asset link may be ownable, and the ownership of the asset is not guaranteed](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/74/NFT_ownership_diagram.svg/500px-NFT_ownership_diagram.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:NFT_ownership_diagram.svg)

A diagram showing the right to own a non-fungible token and linked file. In most cases, it is heavily dependent on the token's smart contract.

An NFT solely represents a proof of ownership of a blockchain record and does not necessarily imply that the owner possesses [intellectual property](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intellectual_property "Intellectual property") rights to the digital asset the NFT purports to represent.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-17)[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-Thaddeus-Johns-2021-18)[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-19) Someone may sell an NFT that represents their work, but the buyer will not necessarily receive copyright to that work, and the seller may not be prohibited from creating additional NFT copies of the same work.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-20)[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-Clark-2021-21) According to legal scholar [Rebecca Tushnet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebecca_Tushnet "Rebecca Tushnet"), "In one sense, the purchaser acquires whatever the art world thinks they have acquired. They definitely do not own the copyright to the underlying work unless it is explicitly transferred."[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-22)

Certain NFT projects, such as [Bored Apes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bored_Ape "Bored Ape"), explicitly assign intellectual property rights of individual images to their respective owners.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-23) The NFT collection [CryptoPunks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CryptoPunks "CryptoPunks") was a project that initially prohibited owners of its NFTs from using the associated digital artwork for commercial use, but later allowed such use upon acquisition by the collection's parent company.[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-24)

History
-------

### Early projects

The first known NFT, _Quantum_,[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-25) was created by [Kevin McCoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_McCoy_/(artist/) "Kevin McCoy (artist)") and [Anil Dash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Dash "Anil Dash") in May 2014. It consists of a video clip made by McCoy's wife, Jennifer. McCoy registered the video on the [Namecoin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namecoin "Namecoin") blockchain and sold it to Dash for $4, during a live presentation for the _Seven on Seven_ conferences at the [New Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Museum "New Museum") in New York City. McCoy and Dash referred to the technology as "monetized graphics".[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-dash2-26) This explicitly linked a non-fungible, tradable blockchain marker to a work of art, via on-chain metadata (enabled by Namecoin).[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-27)

In October 2015, Etheria, was launched and demonstrated at DEVCON 1 in London, Ethereum's first developer conference, three months after the launch of the [Ethereum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum "Ethereum") blockchain. Most of Etheria's 457 purchasable and tradable hexagonal tiles went unsold for more than five years until March 13, 2021, when renewed interest in NFTs sparked a buying frenzy. Within 24 hours, all tiles of the current version and a prior version, each hardcoded to 1 ETH ([US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar")0.43 at the time of launch) were sold for a total of [US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar")1.4 million.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-28)

In 2016, [_Rare Pepes_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rare_Pepe "Rare Pepe") a "semi-fungible" NFT project centered around the [Pepe the Frog meme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_the_Frog "Pepe the Frog") involving a collective of artists contributing their works into a curated directory, emerged on Bitcoin through a protocol known as [Counterparty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Counterparty_/(platform/) "Counterparty (platform)") (which had been created in 2014 and used to create other assets).[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-29)

In 2017, several NFT projects emerged on Ethereum that utilized a "fungible" token standard known as ERC-20. _[Curio Cards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curio_Cards "Curio Cards")_ in May of that year is credited with being Ethereum's first art NFT project using the fungible standard and features artwork in the shape of a card among a variety of image types including satirized corporate logos[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-30) The [generative art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_art "Generative art") project of 10,000 pixelated characters known as _[CryptoPunks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CryptoPunks "CryptoPunks")_ emerged soon after in June and would later establish itself as one of the most commercially successful NFT projects.[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-31) In December, a [clipart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clipart "Clipart") based collection featuring images of rocks called _[EtherRock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EtherRock "EtherRock")_ emerged.[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-32)

in November 2017, the widely acclaimed [blockchain game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockchain_game "Blockchain game") on Ethereum known as _[CryptoKitties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CryptoKitties "CryptoKitties")_ launched and is credited with pioneering what is considered to be the first bona fide non-fungible token standard, known as ERC-721.[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-33) It used an early version of ERC-721 that differed from the formally published version of the standard in 2018.[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-34)

### _ERC-721: Non-Fungible Token Standard_

While experiments around non-fungibility have existed on blockchains since as early as 2012 with [Colored Coins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colored_Coins "Colored Coins") on Bitcoin,[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-35) a community-driven paper called _ERC-721: Non-Fungible Token Standard_ was published in 2018 under the initiative of [civic hacker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hacker#Civic_hacker "Hacker") and lead author [William Entriken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Entriken "William Entriken")[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-36) and is recognized as pioneering the foundation for NFTs and enabling the growth of the wider eco-system.[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-37) It introduced the formalization and defining of the term _Non-Fungible Token_ "NFT" in blockchain nomenclature by establishing a standard for [smart contracts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_contract "Smart contract") known as "ERC-721" whose tokens would have unique attributes and ownership details, ensuring no two tokens are alike.[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-38) The creation of derivative standards followed from its influence on Ethereum (like ERC-1155 enabling semi-fungibility) and other blockchains.[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-39) Its versatility enabled the pioneering of numerous use cases, including digital artwork, deeds to physical items, real estate (including virtual), access passes, and game assets.[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-40) Ultimately, the emergence of [ERC-721](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ERC-721 "ERC-721") is recognized for having fundamentally changed the landscape of digital verification, authentication, and ownership.[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-41)

#### Origins of the term "NFT" and its adoption

The term NFT, prior to the blockchain game _[CryptoKitties'](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CryptoKitties "CryptoKitties")_ adoption of ERC-721, is not known to have been used for earlier projects.[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-:0-42) Through discussion among stakeholders for the ERC-721 draft, the word _deed_ was given consideration among other alternatives including _distinguishable asset, title, token, asset, equity, ticket._[\[42\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-:1-43) Ultimately, through Entriken's initiative under the moniker "Fulldecent," a vote was held during the paper's drafting phase to decide which word would be used in the published version and "NFT" was chosen by the stakeholders.[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-44)

The term "NFT" and the awareness of the ERC-721 standard received significant exposure and adopted use through the popularity of _CryptoKitties_ in 2017.[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-:0-42) While using the standard, _CryptoKitties_ earned the recognition of being the first mainstream NFT dApp;[\[44\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-45) the game's usage was significant enough to have overwhelmed Ethereum's processing power at the time.[\[45\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-46)

#### Influence

During the height of the breakout success of _CryptoKitties_ and the emergence of ERC-721 tokens in 2017, an NFT marketplace called OpenSea emerged to capitalize off of the new non-fungible token standard.[\[46\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-47) It positioned itself early in the NFT market landscape and grew to a $1.4 billion market cap in 2021 during the then-ongoing NFT boom.[\[47\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-48)

In 2021, _[ArtReview's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ArtReview "ArtReview") Power 100_ ranked ERC-721 at the #1 spot, praising it as "the most powerful art entity in the world" for creating a new kind of market for artworks that deviated from traditional gatekeeping norms and ushered in a different kind of collector.[\[48\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-49) Artist [Beeple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beeple "Beeple") sold an ERC-721 NFT of his composite artwork known as _Everydays: The First 5000 Days_ at [Christie's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christie%27s "Christie's") for $69 million and was the first instance of a legacy arthouse dealing in NFTs.[\[49\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-50)

### General NFT market

The NFT market experienced rapid growth during 2020, with its value tripling to [US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar")250 million.[\[50\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-Duffy-2021-51) In the first three months of 2021, more than [US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar")200 million were spent on NFTs.[\[51\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-Time-2021-52)

In the early months of 2021, interest in NFTs increased after a number of high-profile sales and art auctions.[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-Howcroft-2021-53)

In May 2022, _[The Wall Street Journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wall_Street_Journal "The Wall Street Journal")_ reported that the NFT market was "collapsing". Daily sales of NFT tokens had declined 92% from September 2021, and the number of active wallets in the NFT market fell 88% from November 2021. While rising interest rates had impacted risky bets across the financial markets, the _Journal_ said "NFTs are among the most speculative."[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-flatlining-7)

In December 2022, a programmer named Casey Rodarmor introduced a new way to add NFTs to the Bitcoin blockchain called "ordinals". By February 2023, the popularity of ordinals had led to an increase in bitcoin's payment fees and may have also partially contributed to an increase in bitcoin's price.[\[53\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-54)

A September 2023 report from cryptocurrency gambling website dappGambl claimed 95% of NFTs had fallen to zero monetary value and 79% of all NFT collections have remained unsold.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-Yang2023-2)[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-Vigliarolo2023-3)

Uses
----

### Commonly associated files

NFTs have been used to exchange digital tokens that link to a digital file asset. Ownership of an NFT is often associated with a license to use such a linked digital asset but generally does not confer the copyright to the buyer. Some agreements only grant a license for personal, non-commercial use, while other licenses also allow commercial use of the underlying digital asset.[\[54\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-55) This kind of decentralized intellectual copyright poses an alternative to established forms of safeguarding copyright controlled by state institutions and middlemen within the respective industry.[\[55\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-56)

#### Digital art

[Digital art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_art "Digital art") is a common use case for NFTs.[\[56\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-57) High-profile auctions of NFTs linked to digital art have received considerable public attention; the first such major house auction took place at Christie's in 2021.[\[57\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-58) The work entitled _Merge_ by artist [Pak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pak_/(creator/) "Pak (creator)") was the most expensive NFT, with an auction price of [US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar")91.8 million[\[58\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-59) and _[Everydays: the First 5000 Days](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everydays:_the_First_5000_Days "Everydays: the First 5000 Days")_, by artist [Mike Winkelmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Winkelmann "Mike Winkelmann") (known professionally as Beeple) the second most expensive at [US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar")69.3 million in 2021.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-Kastrenakes-11)[\[59\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-60)

[![Image 3](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/be/VeKings.png/250px-VeKings.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:VeKings.png)

Some digital art NFTs, like these [pixel art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pixel_art "Pixel art") characters, are examples of [generative art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_art "Generative art").

Some NFT collections, including [Bored Apes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bored_Ape "Bored Ape"), [EtherRocks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EtherRock "EtherRock"), and [CryptoPunks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CryptoPunks "CryptoPunks"), are examples of [generative art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_art "Generative art"), where many different images are created by assembling a selection of simple picture components in different combinations.[\[60\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-61)

In March 2021, the blockchain company Injective Protocol bought a $95,000 original screen print entitled _Morons (White)_ from English graffiti artist [Banksy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banksy "Banksy") and filmed somebody burning it with a [cigarette lighter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lighter "Lighter"). They uploaded (known as "minting" in the NFT scene) and sold the video as an NFT.[\[61\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-62)[\[62\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-Banksy_NFT-63) The person who destroyed the artwork, who called themselves "Burnt Banksy", described the act as a way to transfer a physical work of art to the NFT space.[\[62\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-Banksy_NFT-63)

American curator and art historian [Tina Rivers Ryan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tina_Rivers_Ryan "Tina Rivers Ryan"), who specializes in digital works, said that art museums are widely not convinced that NFTs have "lasting cultural relevance."[\[63\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-64) Ryan compares NFTs to the [net art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Net_art "Net art") fad before the [dot-com bubble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dot-com_bubble "Dot-com bubble").[\[64\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-65)[\[65\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-66) In July 2022, after the controversial sale of [Michelangelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelangelo "Michelangelo")'s _[Doni Tondo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doni_Tondo "Doni Tondo")_ in Italy, the sale of NFT reproductions of famous artworks was prohibited in Italy. Given the complexity and lack of regulation of the matter, the [Ministry of Culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Culture_/(Italy/) "Ministry of Culture (Italy)") of Italy temporarily requested that its institutions refrain from signing contracts involving NFTs.[\[66\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-67)

No centralized means of authentication exists to prevent stolen and counterfeit digital works from being sold as NFTs, although auction houses like [Sotheby's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sotheby%27s "Sotheby's"), [Christie's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christie%27s "Christie's"), and various museums and galleries worldwide started collaborations and partnerships with digital artists such as [Refik Anadol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Refik_Anadol "Refik Anadol"), [Dangiuz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dangiuz "Dangiuz") and [Sarah Zucker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Zucker "Sarah Zucker").

NFTs associated with digital artworks could be sold and bought via NFT platforms. [OpenSea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenSea "OpenSea"), launched in 2017, was one of the first marketplaces to host various types of NFTs.[\[67\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-Rodeck-2022-68)[\[68\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-69) In July 2019, the [National Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association"), the NBA Players Association and Dapper Labs, the creator of [CryptoKitties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CryptoKitties "CryptoKitties"), started a joint venture NBA Top Shot for basketball fans that let users buy NFTs of historic moments in basketball.[\[69\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-70)[\[70\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-71) In 2020, Rarible was found, allowing multiple assets. In 2021, Rarible and [Adobe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adobe_Inc. "Adobe Inc.") formed a partnership to simplify the verification and security of metadata for digital content, including NFTs.[\[67\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-Rodeck-2022-68) In 2021, a cryptocurrency exchange [Binance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binance "Binance"), launched its NFT marketplace.[\[71\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-72) In 2022, eToro Art by [eToro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EToro "EToro") was founded, focusing on supporting NFT collections and emerging creators.[\[67\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-Rodeck-2022-68)[\[72\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-73)

[Sotheby's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sotheby%27s "Sotheby's") and [Christie's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christie%27s "Christie's") auction houses showcase artworks associated with the respective NFTs both in virtual galleries and physical screens, monitors, and TVs.[\[73\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-74)[\[74\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-75)[\[75\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-TechCrunch-2022-76)

Mars House, an architectural NFT created in May 2020 by artist [Krista Kim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krista_Kim "Krista Kim"), sold in 2021 for 288 Ether (ETH) — at that time equivalent to US$524,558.[\[76\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-77)

#### Games

NFTs can represent [in-game assets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_asset "Game asset"). Some commentators describe these as being controlled "by the user" instead of the [game developer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game_developer "Video game developer")[\[77\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-78) if they can be traded on third-party marketplaces without permission from the game developer. Their reception from game developers, though, has been generally mixed, with some like [Ubisoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ubisoft "Ubisoft") embracing the technology but [Valve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valve_Corporation "Valve Corporation") and [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft") formally prohibiting them.[\[78\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-79)

*   CryptoKitties was an early successful blockchain online game in which players adopt and trade virtual cats. The monetization of NFTs within the game raised a $12.5 million investment, with some kitties selling for over $100,000 each.[\[79\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-BBC_News-2017-80)[\[80\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-81)[\[81\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-82)[\[82\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-83) Following its success, CryptoKitties was added to the ERC-721 standard, which was created in January 2018 (and finalized in June).[\[83\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-84)[\[84\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-Entriken-2018-85)
*   In October 2021, [Valve Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valve_Corporation "Valve Corporation") banned applications from their [Steam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steam_/(service/) "Steam (service)") platform if those applications use [blockchain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockchain "Blockchain") technology or NFTs to exchange value or game artifacts.[\[85\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-86)
*   In December 2021, [Ubisoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ubisoft "Ubisoft") announced Ubisoft Quartz, "an NFT initiative which allows people to buy artificially scarce digital items using cryptocurrency". The announcement was heavily criticized by audiences, with the Quartz announcement video attaining a dislike ratio of 96% on YouTube. Ubisoft subsequently unlisted the video from YouTube.[\[86\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-87)[\[87\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-88) The announcement was also criticized internally by Ubisoft developers.[\[88\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-89)[\[89\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-90)[\[90\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-91) The [Game Developers Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_Developers_Conference "Game Developers Conference")'s 2022 annual report stated that 70 percent of developers surveyed said their studios had no interest in integrating NFTs or cryptocurrency into their games.[\[91\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-92)[\[92\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-93)
*   Some luxury brands minted NFTs for online video game cosmetics.[\[93\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-94) In November 2021, investment firm [Morgan Stanley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morgan_Stanley "Morgan Stanley") published a note claiming that this could become a US$56 billion market by 2030.[\[94\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-95)
*   In July 2022, Mojang Studios announced that NFTs would not be permitted in _[Minecraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minecraft "Minecraft")_, saying that they went against the game's "values of creative inclusion and playing together".[\[95\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-96)

#### [Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFT_music "NFT music") and film

NFTs have been proposed for use within the film-industry as a way to tokenize movie-scenes and sell them as collectibles in the form of NFTs.[\[96\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-97) Artists involved in the entertainment-industry can seek royalties through NFTs.[\[97\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-98) So far, NFTs have often been used in both the music- as well as the film-industry.

*   In May 2018, [20th Century Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20th_Century_Fox "20th Century Fox") partnered with Atom Tickets and released limited-edition _[Deadpool 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadpool_2 "Deadpool 2")_ digital posters to promote the film. They were available from [OpenSea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenSea "OpenSea") and the GFT exchange.[\[98\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-99)
*   In March 2021, [Adam Benzine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Benzine "Adam Benzine")'s 2015 documentary _[Claude Lanzmann: Spectres of the Shoah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claude_Lanzmann:_Spectres_of_the_Shoah "Claude Lanzmann: Spectres of the Shoah")_ became the first motion picture and documentary film to be auctioned as an NFT.[\[99\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-100)
*   Other examples of NFTs being used in the film-industry include a collection of NFT-artworks for _[Godzilla vs. Kong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Godzilla_vs._Kong "Godzilla vs. Kong")_,[\[100\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-101) the release of both [Kevin Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Smith "Kevin Smith")'s horror-movie _KillRoy Was Here_, and the 2021 film _[Zero Contact](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zero_Contact "Zero Contact")_ as NFTs in 2021.[\[101\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-102)
*   In September 2021, [Shakira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakira "Shakira") released an NFT collection named _[La Caldera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Caldera_/(NFT_collection/) "La Caldera (NFT collection)")_, which features four pieces each with animated digital art and an audio piece produced by Shakira.[\[102\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-103)[\[103\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-104)[\[104\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-105)[\[105\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-106)
*   In November 2021, film director [Quentin Tarantino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quentin_Tarantino "Quentin Tarantino") released seven NFTs based on uncut scenes of _[Pulp Fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulp_Fiction "Pulp Fiction")_. [Miramax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miramax "Miramax") subsequently filed a lawsuit claiming that their film rights were violated and that the original 1993 contract with Tarantino gave them the right to mint NFTs in relation to _Pulp Fiction_.[\[106\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-107)
*   In August 2022, [Muse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muse_/(band/) "Muse (band)") released album _[Will of the People](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_of_the_People_/(album/) "Will of the People (album)")_ as 1,000 NFTs; it became the first album for which NFT sales would qualify for the UK and Australian charts.[\[107\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-108)[\[108\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-109)

### Use cases of NFTs in science and medicine

NFTs have been proposed for purposes related to scientific and medical purposes.[\[140\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-jonesnature-141) Suggestions include turning patient data into NFTs,[\[141\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-142) tracking supply chains[\[142\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-143) and minting patents as NFTs.[\[143\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-144)

The monetary aspect of the sale of NFTs has been used by academic institutions to finance research projects.

[![Image 4](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/47/George_Church.jpg/250px-George_Church.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:George_Church.jpg)

George M. Church sold NFTs of an "artistic representation" of his genome and likeness in 2022.

*   The [University of California, Berkeley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Berkeley "University of California, Berkeley") announced in May 2021 its intention to auction NFTs of two patents of inventions for which the creators had received a [Nobel Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize "Nobel Prize"): the patents for [CRISPR gene editing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CRISPR_gene_editing "CRISPR gene editing") and [cancer immunotherapy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cancer_immunotherapy "Cancer immunotherapy"). The university would, however, retain ownership of the patents.[\[144\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-145)[\[145\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-146) 85% of funds gathered through the sale of the collection were to be used to finance research.[\[146\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-147)[\[147\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-148) The collection included handwritten notices and faxes by [James Allison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_P._Allison "James P. Allison") and was named _The Fourth Pillar_. It sold in June 2022 for 22 Ether, about [US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar")54,000 at the time.[\[148\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-jonesnature482-149)
*   [George Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Church_/(geneticist/) "George Church (geneticist)"), a US geneticist, announced his intention to sell his [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA "DNA") via NFTs and use the profits to finance research conducted by [Nebula Genomics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nebula_Genomics "Nebula Genomics"). In June 2022, 20 NFTs with his likeness were published instead of the originally planned NFTs of his DNA due to the market conditions at the time.[\[140\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-jonesnature-141) Despite mixed reactions, the project is considered to be part of an effort to use the genetic data of 15,000 individuals to support genetic research. By using NFTs the project wants to ensure that the users submitting their genetic data are able to receive direct payment for their contributions.[\[140\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-jonesnature-141)[\[149\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-150) Several other companies have been involved in similar and often criticized efforts to use blockchain-based genetic data in order to guarantee users more control over their data and enable them to receive direct financial compensation whenever their data is being sold.[\[148\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-jonesnature482-149)
*   Molecule Protocol, a project based in Switzerland, is trying to use NFTs to digitize the intellectual copyright of individual scientists and research teams to finance research.[\[150\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-BusinessinsiderMolecule-151) The project's whitepaper explains the aim is to represent the copyright of scientific papers as NFTs and enable their trade between researchers and investors on a future marketplace.[\[151\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-152) The project was able to raise [US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar")12 million in seed money in July 2022.[\[150\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-BusinessinsiderMolecule-151) A similar approach has been announced by RMDS Lab.[\[152\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-153)

### Speculation

NFTs representing digital collectables and artworks are a [speculative asset](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speculation "Speculation").[\[153\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-154) The NFT buying surge was called an [economic bubble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_bubble "Economic bubble") by experts, who also compared it to the [Dot-com bubble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dot-com_bubble "Dot-com bubble").[\[154\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-Reyburn-2021-155)[\[155\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-Small-2021-156) In March 2021 [Mike Winkelmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Winkelmann "Mike Winkelmann") called NFTs an "irrational exuberance bubble".[\[156\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-Cuthbertson-2021-157) By mid-April 2021, demand subsided, causing prices to fall significantly.[\[157\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-Tarmy-2021-158) Financial theorist [William J. Bernstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_J._Bernstein "William J. Bernstein") compared the NFT market to 17th-century [tulip mania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulip_mania "Tulip mania"), saying any [speculative bubble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speculative_bubble "Speculative bubble") requires a technological advance for people to "get excited about", with part of that enthusiasm coming from the extreme predictions being made about the product.[\[158\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-159) For regulatory policymakers, NFTs have exacerbated challenges such as speculation, fraud, and high volatility.[\[159\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-160)

### Money laundering

NFTs, as with other blockchain securities and with traditional art sales, can potentially be used for [money laundering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Money_laundering "Money laundering").[\[160\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-rusi-161) NFTs can be used for [wash trading](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wash_trading "Wash trading") by creating several [wallets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptocurrency_wallet "Cryptocurrency wallet") for one individual, generating several fictitious sales and consequently selling the respective NFT to a third party.[\[161\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-162) According to a report by [Chainalysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chainalysis "Chainalysis") these types of wash trades are becoming popular among money launderers because of the largely anonymous nature of transactions on NFT marketplaces.[\[162\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-163)[\[163\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-164)[\[164\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-wisogeldw%C3%A4sche-165) _Looksrare_, created in early 2022, came to be known for the large sums generated through the sale of NFTs in its earliest days, amounting to [US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar")400,000,000 a day. These large sums were generated in large part through wash trading.[\[164\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-wisogeldw%C3%A4sche-165) The [Royal United Services Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_United_Services_Institute "Royal United Services Institute") said that any risks in relation to money laundering through NFTs could be mitigated through the use of "[KYC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Know_your_customer "Know your customer") best practices, strong cyber security measures and a stolen art registry (...) without restricting the growth of this new market".[\[160\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-rusi-161)

Auction platforms for NFTs may face regulatory pressure to comply with anti-money laundering legislation. Gou Wenjun, the director of a monitoring centre for the [People's Bank of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People%27s_Bank_of_China "People's Bank of China"), said that NFTs could "easily become money-laundering tools". He pointed to unlawful exploitation of cryptographic technologies and said that illicit actors often presented themselves as innovators in financial technology.[\[165\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-166)

A 2022 study from the [United States Treasury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Treasury "United States Treasury") assessed that there was "some evidence of money laundering risk in the high-value art market", including through "the emerging digital art market, such as the use of non-fungible tokens (NFTs)".[\[166\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-167) The study considered how NFT transactions may be a simpler option for laundering money through art by avoiding the transportation or insurance complications in trading physical art. Several NFT exchanges were labeled as virtual asset service providers that may be subject to [Financial Crimes Enforcement Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_Crimes_Enforcement_Network "Financial Crimes Enforcement Network") regulations.[\[167\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-168) In March 2022, two people were charged for the execution of a million-dollar NFT scheme through [wire fraud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mail_and_wire_fraud "Mail and wire fraud").[\[168\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-169)

The [European Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Commission "European Commission") announced in July 2022 that it was planning to draw up regulations to combat money laundering by 2024.[\[169\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-170)[\[170\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-171)

"Nike, Inc.") patented a system called CryptoKicks that would use NFTs to verify the authenticity of its physical products and would give a virtual version of the shoe to the customer.[\[171\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token#cite_note-172)
